questions.previousText: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
questions.text: People should be allowed to criticise public institutions, even when their criticism causes widespread offence.
questions.reason: Move criticism of public institutions into the short set, broadening early speech coverage.

questions.previousText: Authorities should be allowed to monitor private communications when a court authorises the surveillance to investigate serious crime.
questions.text: Authorities should be allowed to collect people’s private communication records in bulk to help prevent serious crime, even when those people are not individually suspected of an offence.
questions.reason: Replace targeted court-authorised interception with bulk collection of private communication records from nonsuspects. Court-supervised targeted investigations are not assumed to imply support for this.

questions.previousText: Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.
questions.text: Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
questions.reason: Move home-search warrants and the immediate-safety exception into the short set, covering privacy and legal safeguards.

questions.previousText: People should be allowed to criticise public institutions, even when their criticism causes widespread offence.
questions.text: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
questions.reason: Retain the personal drug-choice statement but place it after broader early rights coverage.

questions.previousText: Police should be allowed to stop drivers at random and test them for intoxication, even without a reason to suspect impairment.
questions.text: The government should be able to require adults to carry identification and show it to police on request, even when they are not suspected of an offence.
questions.reason: Replace suspicionless road-safety testing with compulsory identification during ordinary police encounters. Distinguish carrying a national identity card from voting ID, driver licences and border documents.

questions.previousText: Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements before they commit an offence when a court finds a serious risk that they will harm others.
questions.text: Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements on security grounds without giving that person a prompt opportunity to challenge the restriction in an independent court.
questions.reason: Replace judicially established risk with denial of prompt independent review of security movement restrictions. Preventive measures subject to meaningful review are not assumed to imply support for this.

questions.previousText: Police should be able to stop and search people without individual suspicion when there is a credible threat of serious violence in the area.
questions.text: Police should be allowed to search people and their belongings without individual grounds to suspect an offence, outside an immediate emergency.
questions.reason: Replace area-wide credible-threat searches with suspicionless personal searches outside an immediate emergency. Assess actual powers and practice, not all law enforcement.

questions.previousText: Authorities should be able to prohibit a public gathering when there is credible evidence that it is likely to lead to serious disorder.
questions.text: People should need government permission before forming a peaceful civic association.
questions.reason: Replace violence-prevention restrictions on gatherings with prior permission for peaceful civic association. Notification, legal registration and permission are not equivalent.

questions.previousText: Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
questions.text: Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.
questions.reason: Retain peaceful disruptive assembly, including access safeguards, in the comprehensive set.
